tools.opsecNote: Basic browser detection; reveals current browser info to the site.

tools.name: What Browser?
tools.description: Browser detection service that identifies your browser and offers guidance on updating to current versions; useful for fingerprint verification.
tools.bestFor: Browser version verification, fingerprint audit during OSINT setup
tools.output: Current browser name, version, and update status
tools.opsecNote: Basic browser detection page; use to verify what browser identity is visible before OSINT operations.

tools.name: IP2Proxy
tools.description: Database and lookup service that detects whether an IP address belongs to a proxy, VPN, Tor exit node, or hosting provider to assess anonymization visibility.
tools.bestFor: Checking if your VPN/proxy IP is flagged, verifying anonymization infrastructure quality
tools.output: Proxy type classification (VPN/TOR/hosting/residential), ISP, and country
tools.opsecNote: Passive IP lookup; useful for checking if your exit node IPs are flagged in commercial proxy databases before conducting operations.

tools.name: Privacy Guides
tools.description: Community-maintained guide recommending privacy-respecting software, services, and best practices; covers VPNs, browsers, operating systems, email, and more.
tools.bestFor: Selecting privacy tools, building an OSINT operational security toolkit
tools.output: Curated tool recommendations with evaluation criteria and comparison tables
tools.opsecNote: Reference resource only; no data submission required.

tools.name: Just Delete Me
tools.description: Directory of direct links to account deletion pages for hundreds of online services, rated by deletion difficulty to help with digital footprint removal.
tools.bestFor: Removing digital footprint, deleting OSINT research accounts, cleaning up persona accounts
tools.output: Direct deletion link, difficulty rating (easy/medium/hard/impossible), and deletion instructions
tools.opsecNote: Reference directory only; actual account deletion requires interacting with each service directly.

tools.name: OptOut Credit Prescreen
tools.description: Official US consumer opt-out service operated by major credit bureaus to remove yourself from pre-screened credit and insurance offer lists.
tools.bestFor: Reducing data broker exposure, removing from credit prescreening lists
tools.input: Personal information (SSN, DOB, address) for opt-out request
tools.output: Confirmed opt-out from credit and insurance prescreening offers
tools.opsecNote: Requires submitting real personal information to major credit bureaus; only use for actual personal privacy protection, not during OSINT operations.

tools.name: Credit Freeze
tools.description: Intel Techniques tutorial covering the complete process for freezing credit at all major and specialty bureaus to prevent identity theft and data broker access.
tools.bestFor: Protecting personal identity, hardening against identity theft, reducing data broker profiles
tools.output: Step-by-step credit freeze procedures for all major credit bureaus
tools.opsecNote: Reference guide only; actual freeze requires interacting with each bureau. Recommended as part of comprehensive personal OPSEC.

tools.name: Fake US Identities
tools.description: Generates fake US identity data including names, addresses, SSNs, and driver’s license numbers for test and persona creation purposes.
tools.bestFor: Generating synthetic US identity data for persona creation and testing
tools.output: Synthetic US name, address, SSN, DL number, and biographical data
tools.opsecNote: Generates synthetic data only; using fake SSNs for fraudulent purposes is illegal — intended for legitimate testing and OSINT persona research only.

tools.name: Social Media Fingerprint
tools.description: Browser-based tool that detects which social media platforms you are currently logged into by exploiting cross-origin image loading timing differences.
tools.bestFor: Checking social media session exposure, verifying browser compartmentalization effectiveness
tools.input: No input required (automatic detection via browser)
tools.output: List of social media platforms where active sessions are detected
tools.opsecNote: Detects your active social media sessions locally in-browser; use to verify that OSINT browser profiles are properly isolated from personal accounts.

tools.name: Privacy Tools
tools.description: Privacy-focused tool recommendation site covering encrypted messaging, VPNs, browsers, operating systems, and email providers; now largely redirects to Privacy Guides.
tools.bestFor: Privacy tool discovery, OPSEC toolkit building
tools.output: Curated lists of privacy-respecting tools by category with brief descriptions
tools.opsecNote: Reference site only. Note: privacytools.io has gone through ownership changes; privacyguides.org is the community-maintained successor.

tools.name: Panopticlick
tools.description: EFF browser fingerprinting test (now Cover Your Tracks at coveryourtracks.eff.org) that measures how uniquely identifiable your browser is across the web.
tools.bestFor: Measuring browser fingerprint uniqueness, testing tracker blocking effectiveness
tools.input: No input required (automatic browser fingerprint analysis)
tools.output: Fingerprint uniqueness score, tracker blocking assessment, and detailed fingerprint components
tools.opsecNote: EFF’s canonical browser fingerprint test; visit via Tor/VPN to test anonymization. URL now redirects to coveryourtracks.eff.org.

tools.name: Intel Techniques - Hiding from the Internet
tools.description: Michael Bazzell’s OSINT workbook covering comprehensive personal data removal, digital footprint reduction, and operational security techniques.
tools.bestFor: Personal OPSEC hardening, digital footprint removal, data broker opt-outs
tools.output: Structured workbook with data removal checklists, opt-out links, and privacy hardening steps
tools.opsecNote: Reference document only; no data submitted to download. Highly recommended as an OPSEC foundation guide.

tools.name: The Hitchhiker’s Guide to Online Anonymity
tools.description: Comprehensive, community-maintained guide to online anonymity covering threat modeling, Tor, VMs, operational security, and plausible deniability techniques.
tools.bestFor: Deep OPSEC education, building anonymized OSINT infrastructure, threat modeling
tools.output: Detailed technical guide covering anonymization stack, tools, and practices
tools.opsecNote: Reference document only. One of the most thorough freely available OPSEC guides; regularly updated.

tools.name: Awesome Opt-Out Guide 2026
tools.description: Community GitHub repository compiling data broker opt-out procedures, privacy request templates, and removal links for 2026.
tools.bestFor: Data broker removal, comprehensive opt-out across multiple platforms and services
tools.output: Categorized opt-out links, templates, and step-by-step removal instructions
tools.opsecNote: Reference guide only; actual opt-out requires direct interaction with each service.

tools.name: MAT2 (T)
tools.description: Metadata Anonymisation Toolkit v2 — command-line tool that strips metadata from documents, images, audio files, and archives before sharing to prevent inadvertent disclosure.
tools.bestFor: Removing EXIF/metadata from files before publication, cleaning documents prior to evidence submission or sharing
tools.input: Files (PDF, DOCX, JPEG, PNG, MP3, etc.)
tools.output: Metadata-stripped clean copies of input files
tools.opsecNote: Runs entirely locally; highly recommended before sharing any file collected during OSINT operations.
